identity.name: Afghan Mujahideen
alt_names: Islamic Union of Mujahideen of Afghanistan

land.text: the countryside outside the cities and roads held by the Soviets and the government: 'Almost 80 percent of the country was outside government control'

predecessors.note: A rebel movement, not a state that took a predecessor's whole land; the land is the one the Democratic Republic lost outside its cities.

land.text: the whole country, which the mujahideen coalition governed as the Islamic State of Afghanistan from 28 April 1992

successors.note: The rebels win (rule 5): the movement becomes the government of the same state, so the map continues in afghanistan's colour.

capitals.name: Peshawar (Pakistan), seat of the Afghan Interim Government in exile
capitals.note: 'Headquarters: Peshawar, Pakistan' (infobox); the government 'aimed to base themselves in the city of Jalalabad' but 'the mujahideen failed to win the 1989 Battle of Jalalabad'. Coordinates from the gazetteer.

correction.text: the mujahideen-held countryside, without Kabul where the government sat until 28 April 1992

keyframe_review.note: 586,986 km2 against the infobox 652,864 km2 of Afghanistan (ratio 0.90), consistent in size with 'Almost 80 percent of the country was outside government control' (Soviet–Afghan War page). But the shape contains Kabul, which the government held until 'Fall of Kabul: 28 April 1992', so Kabul is cut out. The shape leaves out most of the northern provinces (gazetteer overlay: Jawzjan 4 of 39 cells, Kunduz 4 of 28, Balkh 21 of 54, Faryab 45 of 73, Baghlan 42 of 63); no page opened says the north was government-held, so it is kept as drawn.

correction.text: the mujahideen-held countryside, without Kabul where the government sat until 28 April 1992

keyframe_review.note: 644,005 km2 (ratio 0.99): the whole country, including Kabul, and 202 grid cells more than the 1987 shape (the northern provinces). 'By the beginning of 1991, the government controlled only 10 percent of Afghanistan' and 'the government lost control of the countryside' (Democratic Republic page), so a whole-country rebel shape is right for the countryside only; Kabul is cut out. The enlargement of 1990 has no page.

correction.text: not a separate rebel shape: draw as afghanistan (Islamic State of Afghanistan) from 28 April 1992 to 1995

keyframe_review.note: 643,926 km2, identical to the Afghanistan outline of 2006. From 28 April 1992 ('Fall of Kabul: 28 April 1992'; the page lists the Islamic State of Afghanistan as successor) the mujahideen are the government of the state, so the outline belongs to afghanistan (its keyframe afghanistan_1992). The Mujahideen page adds that after the Peshawar Accords the factions 'could not establish a functional united government' and 'began to fight each other': a civil war inside one state, not a rebel state with its own land.

correction.text: unrelated to the Afghan mujahideen: an outline over northern and north-eastern Syria for 2014-2023, to be given to a Syrian rebel or Islamic State dossier; no page opened identifies it

keyframe_review.note: 68,889 km2, 2014-2023, an outline in Syria (bbox 35.8-42.4E, 32.4-37.3N), not in Afghanistan. A gazetteer overlay on Natural Earth provinces puts it over Hasakah (94% of the province's cells), Aleppo (78%), Deir ez-Zor (61%), Idlib (48%), Dar'a (43%) and Raqqa (35%), almost none over Hamah (1 of 37 cells) and none over Homs, Latakia, Tartus or Damascus. No page opened says what it is: the Syrian civil war page never uses the word 'mujahideen' and describes, for 2014, the Islamic State holding 'Eastern Syria', a Kurdish-led coalition (YPG/SDF), and later Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham in Idlib 'from 2017 until 2024'. The movement of the Afghan dossier has nothing to do with it. It should be a Syrian dossier of its own (me-10 / the Syria group), not drawn as Afghan mujahideen.

correction.text: unrelated to the Afghan mujahideen: the same Syrian outline, to be given to a Syrian dossier

keyframe_review.note: Same 68,889 km2 Syrian outline as 2014-2023. The Syrian civil war page says that on 8 December 2024 'Bashar al-Assad fled to Moscow as Homs fell to HTS', which post-dates and does not match a fixed north-eastern outline. Not Afghan; see mujahideen_2014.

region.text: the countryside: 'Almost 80 percent of the country was outside government control'; the page names no province

ledger.note: 1979: the Afghan mujahideen rise against the Soviet-backed government and the invading Soviets. War dates 25 December 1979 to 15 February 1989 (infobox); 'Almost 80 percent of the country was outside government control'. The Islamic Unity page says the parties' bloc 'had de facto existed as a political bloc since May 1979' and was formed as an alliance in 1988 (the Mujahideen page: May 1985 in a footnote). Cliopatria's shapes begin only in 1987.

region.text: the countryside outside the cities and roads

ledger.note: 1979: guerrilla war against the government's cities and roads. 'Soviet troops occupied Afghanistan's major cities and all main arteries of communication'; the rebels held the rest.

February 1989: the seven Sunni parties form the Afghan Interim Government. 'In February 1989 the seven Sunni mujahideen factions formed an Afghan Interim Government (AIG) in Peshawar.' The page adds 'The AIG became a failure, partly because it could not solve the differences between the factions.'
February 1989: the government in exile sits at Peshawar, Pakistan (infobox headquarters) after 'the groups attempted to form a coalition government in exile from Peshawar'.

region.text: the countryside and now the capital

ledger.note: 28 April 1992: the mujahideen enter Kabul. Najibullah 'was forced to resign by 4 of his generals' on 14 April; infobox 'Fall of Kabul: 28 April 1992'.

region.text: the whole country, which passes to the Islamic State of Afghanistan

ledger.note: April 1992: the mujahideen win and become the Islamic State of Afghanistan (successor named on the page; Afghanistan page infobox 'Islamic State: 28 April 1992'). The land is the whole country (Cliopatria's 1992 shape, 643,926 km2), which the page does not outline.

wars.name: Soviet–Afghan War

zones.text: 'Almost 80 percent of the country was outside government control'

wars.outcome: Infobox result 'Afghan mujahideen victory', 25 December 1979 to 15 February 1989; the last Soviet column left on 15 February 1989.

wars.name: Battle of Jalalabad (1989)

zones.text: Jalalabad, where the Afghan Interim Government 'aimed to base themselves'

wars.outcome: The government 'rallied to break the siege of Jalalabad' in March 1989, its first major victory in years; 'the mujahideen failed to win the 1989 Battle of Jalalabad' (Islamic Unity page). No border changed.
wars.note: Dated 'March 1989' on the Soviet–Afghan War page.

wars.name: Afghan civil war (1989-1992)

zones.text: the countryside; 'By the beginning of 1991, the government controlled only 10 percent of Afghanistan'

wars.outcome: The Afghan government lost the countryside, Najibullah resigned on 14 April 1992 and Kabul fell on 28 April 1992; the Islamic State of Afghanistan followed.
wars.note: The war's own Wikipedia article was not opened; this entry rests on the Democratic Republic page.

certainty.note: The rebels held the countryside around Soviet and government cities and roads; no page gives a line, only shares ('almost 80 percent', 'only 10 percent' for the government in 1991).

notes: Cliopatria's 'Mujahideen' (1987..2024, Q42759) is two unrelated things: shapes 1987, 1990 and 1992 are the Afghan resistance and, from 1992, the state itself; shapes 2014 and 2024 are an outline in northern and north-eastern Syria. This dossier keeps the Afghan movement as a rebel (type rebel) from 25 December 1979, the first day of the war, to 28 April 1992, when the mujahideen took Kabul; mujahideen_1992 is marked wrong because from that date the outline is the state afghanistan (keyframe afghanistan_1992). The Syrian shapes (mujahideen_2014 and mujahideen_2024, 68,889 km2) are marked wrong. No page opened identifies them: the Mujahideen page says 'Various Islamic groups, often referred to as mujahideen and jihadists, have participated in the Syrian civil war' and the Syrian civil war page never uses the word. The overlay (Hasakah 94%, Aleppo 78%, Deir ez-Zor 61%, Idlib 48%, Dar'a 43%, Raqqa 35% of cells) matches opposition-, Islamic State- and Kurdish-held Syria in no single year, so a Syria group (me-10) should decide whether it is the Syrian opposition, the Islamic State, or a Cliopatria stand-in, and write a dossier or drop it. I did not create a dossier for it because nothing opened names it. Not settled: when the rebels first held land (1979-1986 has no Cliopatria shape), why the 1990 shape adds the northern provinces (Jawzjan, Kunduz, Balkh, Faryab, Baghlan), and the factional fiefs after 1992. The government's side of 1987-1991 is in afghanistan (nominal whole country, contested). Five pages opened, the budget; the Afghan Interim Government URL served the 2001 Interim Administration, so the 1989 government's details come from the Mujahideen and Islamic Unity pages. Wikipedia's article on the war of 1989-1992 was not opened.
